veranderings.blok: Drie maniere om klank te maak
veranderings.rede: 'sorteer' has no object here, so the sentence reads incomplete; naming what is sorted makes it clear.

veranderings.blok: Geskud: die hosho en die kokonratels
veranderings.voor: 'n ratel van die Shona van Zimbabwe
veranderings.na: 'n ratel van die Shona in Zimbabwe
veranderings.rede: Avoids the double 'van ... van' and matches the parallel 'die VhaVenda in Limpopo' in the ngoma block.

veranderings.voor: Die riwwe gee elkeen 'n kort tik
veranderings.na: Elkeen van die riwwe gee 'n kort tik
veranderings.rede: 'gee elkeen 'n kort tik' can be read as 'give everyone a tap'; putting 'elkeen' first removes the ambiguity.

veranderings.voor: kom in baie lande voor, ook in Afrika
veranderings.na: kom in baie dele van die wêreld voor, ook in Afrika
veranderings.rede: Afrika is a continent, not a country, so 'baie lande ... ook in Afrika' does not hang together logically.

veranderings.blok: Elke vraag gee sy eie groepe
veranderings.rede: 'Neem' for an imagined example echoes English 'take'; 'Dink aan' is the natural Afrikaans way to set up a thought example.

veranderings.blok: Elke vraag gee sy eie groepe
veranderings.na: val hulle nou in verskillende groepe
veranderings.rede: 'uitmekaar val' means to break apart physically, so a child can read that the tins fall to pieces.

veranderings.blok: Wat elke instrument aan die stuk doen
veranderings.voor: Wat elke instrument aan die stuk doen
veranderings.na: Wat elke instrument in die stuk doen
veranderings.rede: 'aan die stuk doen' reads like 'doing something to the piece'; 'in die stuk' is the natural preposition for a part in music.
'ding' is vague and childish in a definition; 'oppervlak' says where the ridges stand out.

veranderings.voor: hoeveel telle in elke maat is
veranderings.na: hoeveel telle daar in elke maat is
veranderings.rede: An existential clause in Afrikaans needs 'daar'; without it the sentence sounds clipped.

veranderings.na: sonder dat jy van plek verander
veranderings.rede: 'verskuif' used of a person without an object is unnatural; 'van plek verander' is clear and echoes the 'beweging' definition.

vlae.rede: 'gevonde voorwerp' is an art term (from 'found object') that a Grade 4 learner may not know, and the block never explains it. If it is a CAPS term, keep it. If not, a plainer heading might suit better, but choosing one means guessing the intent, so I have not proposed a change.
This headword is written without hyphens while the matching 'roep-en-antwoord' has them. The two parallel terms are written differently, and a headword cannot be changed by the language step.
